[2026-15666: lines 1828-2037 of 4700, FR page 49244]
  1828  I. Collective Bargaining, Grievance Arbitration, and CBAs
  1829  
  1830      Commenters 0962, 1025, 1092, 0928, and 1217 objected to the 
  1831  proposal's treatment of negotiated grievance procedures, arbitration, 
  1832  and collective bargaining agreements. These commenters argued that the 
  1833  Federal Service Labor-Management Relations Statute protects negotiated 
  1834  grievance and arbitration procedures; that RIF matters are not among 
  1835  the matters excluded from negotiated grievance procedures under 5 
  1836  U.S.C. 7121(c); that questions of arbitrability should be resolved 
  1837  through negotiated grievance procedures; and that OPM may not use a 
  1838  governmentwide regulation to eliminate existing collective-bargaining 
  1839  rights or union representation. Other commenters, including 0221, 0584, 
  1840  0587, 0591, and 0621, asserted that the proposal would unlawfully 
  1841  supersede existing CBAs, while commenters 0386 and 1004 requested a 
  1842  clearer legal basis for OPM's position. Commenters 0049, 0092, 0483, 
  1843  and others objected as a policy matter to any prospective limitation on 
  1844  negotiated RIF appeal procedures.
  1845      OPM has considered these comments and has decided to finalize the 
  1846  regulatory text as initially proposed, with some modifications. The 
  1847  final Sec.  351.901(c) provides that the procedures in part 351 are the 
  1848  ``sole and exclusive means'' of appealing a RIF action, and matters 
  1849  relating to such actions may not be raised under a negotiated grievance 
  1850  procedure or contested through grievance arbitration, but employees are 
  1851  not otherwise impeded from filing a complaint, appeal, or other matter 
  1852  within the jurisdiction of the EEOC, an Inspector General, MSPB, DOL 
  1853  VETS, or OSC.
  1854      OPM continues to conclude that a single governmentwide process for 
  1855  direct RIF-compliance appeals is necessary to ensure uniform 
  1856  interpretation and application of part 351. RIF appeals under part 351 
  1857  involve governmentwide rules governing competitive areas, competitive 
  1858  levels, retention standing, order of release, assignment rights, 
  1859  notice, and related requirements. Allowing agencies to create or 
  1860  bargain for parallel direct appeal mechanisms for the same RIF-
  1861  compliance claim would undermine the consistency, finality, and 
  1862  efficiency the final rule is designed to achieve.
  1863      This conclusion is consistent with 5 U.S.C. 7117(a)(1). That 
  1864  provision states that the duty to bargain extends only ``to the extent 
  1865  not inconsistent with any Federal law or any governmentwide rule or 
  1866  regulation,'' and, for matters that are the subject of a rule or 
  1867  regulation, applies only where the rule or regulation is not 
  1868  governmentwide. 5 U.S.C. 7117(a)(1). This final rule is a 
  1869  governmentwide regulation: it applies across agencies to appeals of 
  1870  covered RIF actions under part 351. To that end, it firmly and 
  1871  completely limits the flexibility of agencies to provide processes not 
  1872  contemplated by this rule, including grievance arbitration. See U.S. 
  1873  Dep't of Treasury, I.R.S. v. FLRA, 996 F.2d 1246, 1250 (D.C. Cir. 1993) 
  1874  (IRS) (5 U.S.C. 7117(a)(1) ``permits the government to pull a subject 
  1875  out of the bargaining process by issuing a governmentwide rule that 
  1876  creates a regime inconsistent with bargaining,'' including where a 
  1877  regulation ``sets out an exclusive method of resolving any claims''). 
  1878  Accordingly, agencies may not bargain for a claims-channeling process 
  1879  that conflicts with the final rule's designation of part 351 as the 
  1880  sole and exclusive means of directly appealing a RIF action.
  1881      OPM is not persuaded by commenters' argument that 5 U.S.C. 
  1882  7121(a)(1) overrides this conclusion. Section 7121(a)(1) requires CBAs 
  1883  to provide procedures for settlement of grievances, including questions 
  1884  of arbitrability, and makes those procedures the exclusive 
  1885  administrative procedures for grievances that fall within their 
  1886  coverage. But that provision must be read together with section 
  1887  7117(a)(1), which limits the duty to bargain where the matter is 
  1888  inconsistent with Federal law or a governmentwide rule or regulation. 
  1889  The broad definition of ``grievance'' in 5 U.S.C. 7103(a)(9) likewise 
  1890  does not displace section 7117(a)(1). The fact that RIFs are not listed 
  1891  in section 7121(c) does not mean parties may bargain for an alternative 
  1892  direct RIF appeal procedure that conflicts with a governmentwide 
  1893  regulation establishing a single appeal process.
  1894      The D.C. Circuit Court of Appeal's decision in IRS addressed 
  1895  exactly this issue. The court held that a union proposal that would 
  1896  permit grievances over contracting out was non-negotiable as it 
  1897  conflicted with OMB Circular A-76, a government-wide rule that 
  1898  prescribed the exclusive method for resolving disputes over contracting 
  1899  decisions. The court thus held that Circular A-76 prohibited bargaining 
  1900  over conflicting appeals processes. The final Sec.  351.901(c) 
  1901  similarly prohibits creating an alternative RIF appeals process through 
  1902  collective bargaining.
  1903      OPM also disagrees with Commenter 0962's assertion that section 
  1904  7121(a)(1) has primacy over section 7117(a)(1). Sections 7103, 7117, 
  1905  and 7121 are part of the same statutory scheme and must be read 
  1906  together. Section 7121 establishes negotiated grievance procedures for 
  1907  matters properly within a CBA's coverage; section 7117(a)(1) defines 
  1908  the outer boundary of the bargaining obligation where Federal law or a 
  1909  governmentwide regulation has occupied the field. Reading section 7121 
  1910  to require negotiated grievance arbitration of direct RIF appeals 
  1911  notwithstanding section 7117 would effectively nullify section 
  1912  7117(a)(1) for any matter that could be characterized as a grievance. 
  1913  In IRS the D.C. Circuit expressly rejected that statutory construction. 
  1914  OPM accordingly declines to adopt that reading.
  1915      Nor is this final rule merely a restatement of management rights 
  1916  under 5 U.S.C. 7106. Section 7106 preserves agency authority, subject 
  1917  to subsection (b), to determine mission, budget, organization, number 
  1918  of employees, internal security practices, and to lay off and retain 
  1919  employees, while also preserving bargaining over procedures and 
  1920  appropriate arrangements in appropriate circumstances. 5 U.S.C. 
  1921  7106(a), (b). The final rule does not simply repeat those management 
  1922  rights. It establishes a detailed governmentwide appellate process 
  1923  governing who may appeal, the burden of proof, filing deadlines, 
  1924  agency-record production, service, replies, inspection of the appellate 
  1925  record, representation, adjudication, protective orders, 
  1926  reconsideration, Director review, and finality.
  1927  
  1928  [[Page 49245]]
  1929  
  1930      For that reason, commenters' reliance on Office of Personnel 
  1931  Management v. FLRA, 864 F.2d 165 (D.C. Cir. 1988), is misplaced. In 
  1932  that case, the court addressed whether a governmentwide regulation that 
  1933  merely restated management rights could displace bargaining 
  1934  obligations. This rule does not merely restate a management right; it 
  1935  creates a specific, comprehensive appeal procedure for covered RIF 
  1936  actions. The final rule is therefore more closely aligned with the 
  1937  principle that a governmentwide rule may establish an exclusive method 
  1938  for resolving a particular category of claims, rather than simply 
  1939  invoking management rights at a high level of generality.
  1940      OPM also considered comments invoking the general purposes of the 
  1941  FSLMRS, including 5 U.S.C. 7101(a)(1), which recognizes that collective 
  1942  bargaining safeguards the public interest, contributes to the effective 
  1943  conduct of public business, and facilitates amicable dispute 
  1944  resolution. OPM does not dispute those principles. But section 7101 
  1945  must be read with the rest of chapter 71, including section 7117(a)(1), 
  1946  and with section 7101(b)'s direction that chapter 71 be interpreted 
  1947  consistently with the requirements of an effective and efficient 
  1948  Government. Those provisions support, rather than preclude, a 
  1949  governmentwide rule establishing one uniform process for direct RIF-
  1950  compliance appeals and prohibiting grievances over matters pertaining 
  1951  to RIF appeals.
  1952      In addition to the benefits of maintaining a uniform process for 
  1953  direct RIF-compliance appeals, OPM believes it is beneficial to 
  1954  foreclose grievance arbitration in particular as a forum for 
  1955  adjudicating RIF appeals. As OPM explained in the proposed rule, the 
  1956  arbitrators who adjudicate Federal-sector grievances are private 
  1957  contractors who typically do not have a background in agency operations 
  1958  or Federal employment law. This makes them ill-suited to evaluate 
  1959  potentially complex issues involved in arbitration appeals. OPM is 
  1960  aware of multiple studies showing that, across multiple 
  1961  administrations, the FLRA overturns arbitral awards at a high rate.\24\ 
  1962  The author of one of these studies, himself an arbitrator, concluded 
  1963  that ``Federal sector arbitration is more complex than private sector 
  1964  arbitration. The federal field is full of land mines in the form of 
  1965  laws with which federal sector arbitrators may be less familiar.'' \25\ 
  1966  Foreclosing grievance arbitration ensures adjudication will be handled 
  1967  by MSAC employees with specialized legal and subject matter expertise 
  1968  who are less likely to make reversible errors.
  1969  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1970  
  1971      \24\ See James Sherk, ``Federal Union Arbitrators Frequently 
  1972  Misapply the Law,'' (Aug. 2, 2023), https://www.americafirstpolicy.com/issues/expert-insight-federal-union-arbitrators-frequently-misapply-the-law (finding that between 2019 
  1973  and 2023 over 40 percent of arbitration awards were overturned or 
  1974  remanded upon appeal); see also Helburn, B. (2019). The Trump FLRA: 
  1975  Fair or foul (Helburn), at 6. https://cdn.govexec.com/media/gbc/docs/pdfs_edit/060619ew1.pdf (finding the FLRA set aside or remanded 
  1976  arbitration awards 80, 50, and 43 percent of the time in a sampling 
  1977  of cases arising under the Trump 45, Obama, and George W. Bush 
  1978  Administrations, respectively).
  1979      \25\ Helburn at 10.
  1980  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1981  
  1982      Additionally, under 5 U.S.C. 7122(a) arbitral awards concerning RIF 
  1983  appeals are subject to FLRA review. This review can be protracted, 
  1984  especially if the FLRA loses a quorum or the FLRA has a vacancy and the 
  1985  remaining members deadlock.\26\ Authorizing grievance arbitration over 
  1986  RIF actions would thus create a protracted second level of appeals that 
  1987  would undermine the expeditious resolution of cases. OPM declines to 
  1988  adopt this approach.
  1989  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1990  
  1991      \26\ The FLRA has reported that in FY 2024 the average age of 
  1992  pending (not decided) arbitration cases undergoing review was 307 
  1993  days. See U.S. Federal Labor Relations Authority, Congressional 
  1994  Budget Justification 2026, at 19. https://www.flra.gov/system/files/webfm/FLRA%20Agency-wide/Public%20Affairs/CBJ/FLRA%20FY26%20CBJ%20-%20Final.pdf.
  1995  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1996  
  1997      OPM also clarifies that the final rule does not retroactively 
  1998  invalidate existing CBAs or purport to adjudicate particular CBA 
  1999  disputes in this rulemaking. To the extent commenters argued that the 
  2000  proposal would automatically vitiate existing agreements mid-term, OPM 
  2001  does not adopt that position in the final rule. Rather, when agreements 
  2002  are renegotiated, this governmentwide rule will limit agencies' duty 
  2003  and ability to bargain for provisions that create a direct RIF appeal 
  2004  process inconsistent with part 351. Questions concerning the effect of 
  2005  particular existing agreement provisions, negotiability disputes, or 
  2006  unfair-labor-practice allegations remain matters for resolution under 
  2007  chapter 71 by the appropriate forum.
  2008      OPM also disagrees that the final rule eliminates union 
  2009  representation. Final Sec.  351.904(a) provides that an appellant may 
  2010  select a representative of the appellant's choice to assist in 
  2011  preparing and presenting an appeal, provided the appellant submits a 
  2012  written designation of representative for the specific appeal. That 
  2013  representative may be a union representative where otherwise 
  2014  appropriate. Separate limitations on official time, duty status, and 
  2015  reimbursement for Federal employee representatives are addressed in the 
  2016  representation and official-time discussion.
  2017      OPM therefore declines to revise the final rule to permit 
  2018  negotiated grievance arbitration to serve as an alternative direct 
  2019  appeal mechanism for covered RIF actions under part 351. The final rule 
  2020  establishes a uniform OPM process for direct RIF appeals while 
  2021  preserving collateral statutory matters in the forums Congress or 
  2022  applicable law has designated. This approach gives effect to both the 
  2023  RIF appeal framework in part 351 and the limits on bargaining imposed 
  2024  by 5 U.S.C. 7117(a)(1), while avoiding retroactive invalidation of 
  2025  existing CBAs in this rulemaking.

summary.text: Analyzing OPM admin leave rules and RIF requirements, confirming no impact on standing or appeal rights and noting noncompliance with 402(c) advance approval.Evaluating RIF compliance items 3 through 9 against 5 CFR part 351, noting cutoff and rating inconsistencies.Completing RIF register scoring and displacement eligibility checks for GS-13 employees.Resolving sequential displacement order and lowest-reduction assignments for released employees.

Q2.answer: (a) Values: Level 5=7, Level 4=5, Level 3=3, Level 2/1=0, 351.503(a)(1). Three most recent ratings in 4 years before 2026-09-03 notices, 351.503(c)(1); missing-rating rules 351.503(f). Abbott (career, subgroup I): 7+5+5=17, vet 0 (Subgroup B), total 17. Bianchi (career, I): 5+0+3=8, +5 (30%+, 351.504(a)(1), AD), total 13. Q4.answer: (a) Notices issued 2026-09-03; 4-year period prior to issuance, 351.503(c)(1). All five ratings are in period, but only the three most recent count: 2026-08-10 Level 5 (7), 2025-11-14 Level 3 (3), 2024-11-15 Level 3 (3) = 13. (b) Cutoff 45 days before 2026-09-03: 2026-09-03 minus 45 days = 2026-07-20 (31 days back to 2026-08-03, plus 14 more to 2026-07-20). A rating signed and given to the employee on 2026-07-15 (before cutoff) but not entered in the register office's system until 2026-08-15 was not on record by the 2026-07-20 cutoff and cannot be used. (e) No rating of record in the 4 years: 351.503(f)(1) bases credit on the modal rating as defined in 351.203 for the pattern applying to the employee's position of record, and 351.503(b)(3) ratings from a non-part-430 system count only if the agency in its sole discretion treats them as equivalent ratings of record, which by assumption it does not. The point value cannot be computed from the 2026 documents, which do not print a definition or value for "modal rating" - the formula is 3 x (point value of the modal rating for that pattern).

Q5.answer: (a)(i) Notices issued 2026-08-28, before the 2026-09-02 effective date, so the earlier rules apply (2026-15665, DATES). Both career, tenure group I, subgroup B; ranking by adjusted SCD. The 2026-10-15 rating therefore does not change standing (the later date only moves the effective date from 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-30). The error-correction duty in 351.507(c) is unaffected but no error is shown. Q6.answer: (a) Jordan meets 351.701(a): competitive service tenure group employee, current annual rating of record Level 2 (minimally satisfactory) or higher. Assignment rights under 351.701(b): position held by an employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group, not more than 3 grades (or grade intervals) below, qualified under 351.702/703. One-grade interval progression from GS-13: GS-12, GS-11, GS-10 are 1-3 intervals below; GS-9 is 4 below and outside the limit. (1) Ellis GS-12, lower standing - available. (2) Frank GS-11, lower - available. (3) Gale GS-10, lower - available. (4) Hana GS-9, lower but 4 grades below - not available. (5) Ito GS-12, higher standing - not available, 351.701(b)(1). (6) Kim GS-12 part-time - not available, offered position must have the same type of work schedule, 351.701(a). (7) Lund GS-12, different competitive area - not available, must be in the same competitive area, 351.701(a). The agency must offer the position requiring no reduction or the least possible reduction in representative rate among eligible positions, 351.701(a) - the GS-12 held by Ellis. (b) Preference eligible with 30%+ disability: the limit in 351.701(b)(2) becomes 5 grades, so Hana's GS-9 (4 below) becomes available as an assignment-right position, but the mandatory offer remains Ellis's GS-12 as the least-reduction position. (c) Current rating Level 1: 351.701(a) requires Level 2 or higher; Jordan has no assignment right and no position must be offered. (d) Excepted service: 351.701(a) by its terms applies to a competitive service tenure group employee; there is no mandatory assignment right. Under 351.705(a) an agency may at its discretion adopt provisions giving excepted service competing employees assignment rights on the same basis - discretionary only unless the agency has adopted such a provision. (e) The 2026 documents eliminate "bumping" and "retreating" as separate concepts and replace them with a single assignment right to a position held by a lower-standing employee in the same tenure group, 91 FR 49178 summary item 12 and 49204; the former 351.701(d) restriction preventing a Level 2 employee from taking a position held by a higher-rated employee was eliminated, 91 FR 49204, because standing is now the augmented total, not the rating alone. The old handbook's distinction and its Level 2 bar do not reflect the amended rules, although the Level 2 threshold in 351.701(a) remains.
Q6.uncertainty: Whether an agency has adopted discretionary excepted-service assignment rights under 351.705(a) in case (d) cannot be determined from the Federal Register documents.

Q7.answer: (a) Notice issued 2026-08-31, before 2026-09-02: the MSPB hears the appeal. OPM's appeals rule applies only to a RIF action for which the agency issues the specific RIF notice on or after 2026-09-02 (2026-15666 DATES), and the MSPB stated it will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals where the agency's RIF notice was issued before that date (2026-16456 at 91 FR 51997). Documents bearing on the answer: 2026-15666 (OPM RIF Appeals final rule, 91 FR 49230) and 2026-16456 (MSPB Appellate Jurisdiction Update II, 91 FR 51997); the applicability statement in 2026-15666 at 91 FR 49232-49233 is to the same effect. (b) Notice issued 2026-10-19, on/after 2026-09-02: appeal lies to OPM, not the MSPB, 351.901(a). She must file through the electronic filing system identified on OPM's website, 351.902(a),(c). Counting, 351.902(b): appeal within 30 calendar days from the effective date; first day counted is the day after the effective date. Effective Friday 2026-12-18; day 1 = 2026-12-19; day 30 = 2027-01-17 (13 days to 2026-12-31 plus 17 days in January). 2027-01-17 is a Sunday, so under 351.902(b)(1) the period includes the first workday after that date, 2027-01-18, and the appeal is timely if electronically filed by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on that day. (c) She must prove by a preponderance of the evidence: (1) timeliness, (2) OPM jurisdiction, (3) the agency failed to comply with an applicable statute or OPM regulation governing RIFs under part 351, and (4) prejudice - the failure caused her to be subjected to the action or to lose a materially more favorable outcome, 351.901(b). She is not entitled to a hearing as of right: review is based solely on the developed written record unless OPM determines a hearing is necessary and efficient (record insufficient on a material fact, or material witness-credibility dispute), 351.905(c). (d) The rule bars it: 351.901(c)(1)-(2) makes subpart I procedures the sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action under part 351 and provides a RIF action and any matter relating to its appeal "may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration." The preamble at 91 FR 49244-49245 says the rule does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs or adjudicate particular CBA disputes in the rulemaking; when agreements are renegotiated, the governmentwide rule limits the duty and ability to bargain for a conflicting direct RIF appeal process, and questions about existing provisions remain for chapter 71 resolution. (e) No: 351.901(c)(4) - "A party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under this subpart." (f) Yes, she may still appeal: 351.902(b)(3) allows an employee who, before expiration of the filing period, timely filed a complaint/appeal/matter within the independent jurisdiction of an entity in 351.901(c) (OSC is listed) to file a RIF appeal within 30 calendar days after the collateral decision becomes final and is no longer subject to further administrative review, if it materially affects retention standing, order of release, assignment rights or other part 351 rights, as determined by OPM in its sole and exclusive discretion. On the facts - OSC complaint filed before the deadline, final decision 2027-03-10 correcting the rating in a way that would have changed standing - the RIF appeal must be filed within 30 calendar days after 2027-03-10, i.e. by 2027-04-09, 11:59 p.m. ET (subject to the weekend/holiday rule if that date is a Saturday, Sunday or Federal holiday). (g) The deciding provision is the applicability/DATES provision of the OPM appeals rule: 2026-15666, DATES at 91 FR 49230 - "This final rule applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026" - restated in the preamble at 91 FR 49232-49233; the MSPB's parallel statement is at 91 FR 51997.
Q7.uncertainty: Whether 2027-01-18 is a Federal holiday (which would move the (b) deadline to the next workday) is not stated in the Federal Register documents; the count to the first workday after Sunday 2027-01-17 is as stated. The (f) deadline assumes OPM determines the OSC decision materially affects her rights, as the scenario stipulates it would have changed standing.

Q8.answer: (a) The version in force today (2026-11-14) is the pre-2026-10-19 text of 351.806, which the main 2026 RIF rule did not amend; its full text is not printed in the 2026 documents. As described in the administrative-leave rule's preamble, the former paragraph (a) provided the employee would remain in duty status during the notice period "when possible," 91 FR 65926, 65933. The adopted but not yet in-force version, 2026-21320 at 91 FR 65939, effective 2026-11-18, revises 351.806 to: (a) "Under ordinary circumstances, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period"; (b) nothing precludes the agency from placing the employee on administrative leave for all or part of the notice period when the agency determines it is appropriate and consistent with part 630, subpart N; (c) in an emergency lack of work or funds, the agency may place the employee on annual leave with or without consent, on leave without pay with consent, or in nonpay status without consent. (b) Under adopted 351.806(b) employee consent is not required for administrative leave; the agency's determination of appropriateness and consistency with 630 subpart N control. Companion 630.1403(c)(10) at 91 FR 65940 permits administrative leave for RIF-affected employees between receipt of the RIF notice and separation when the agency determines it is in the Government's best interests, "subject to Governmentwide limits established by OPM and agency limits" - the printed text states no fixed number of days for this use. (c) OPM states that its policy guidance already provided that an authorized agency official may provide administrative leave between an employee's receipt of a notice of involuntary separation and the effective date of that separation, and that the new paragraph (b) is consistent with that guidance, 91 FR 65926. (d) No. OPM states the new provisions address only whether an employee may be placed in paid non-duty status during the notice period, do not alter the substantive or procedural requirements governing RIF, and do not authorize bypassing RIF competition, retention registers or appeal rights, 91 FR 65926; retention standing is fixed as of receipt of the notice, 351.507(a).
Q8.basis: 2026-21320 at 91 FR 65924-65940: DATES (eff. 2026-11-18), preamble at 65926 and 65933, regulatory text 351.806 at 65939 and 630.1403(c)(10) at 65940; 2026-15665 regulatory text (no amendment to 351.806) at 91 FR 49218-49227.
Q8.uncertainty: The full text of the currently in-force 351.806 is not printed in the 2026 documents and is not supplied from memory; only the former "when possible" duty-status formulation is described in the 2026 preamble.

Q9.answer: (1) Does not comply in part. Designation/approval by the agency head's designee, not below headquarters level, and chart publication comply with 351.402(b)(1). But the area was designated 2026-08-17, 57 days before notices were issued 2026-10-13, i.e. within 90 days before issuing specific RIF notices; 351.402(c) requires the agency to submit a description and bona fide organizational-basis statement to OPM for approval in advance of the RIF. Nothing was sent to OPM. Required: prior OPM approval with the description and statement, made readily available. (2) In order. A career-conditional employee serving an initial probationary period is not a competing employee, 351.202(d)(2)(ii); the agency may retain such an employee while releasing a competing employee, 351.202(d)(3). (3) Does not comply. "Initial probationary period" does not include the supervisory/managerial probationary period under part 315 subpart I, 351.203; the preamble confirms a career-tenure employee on supervisory probation is included in the RIF in the supervisory position and is not excluded, 91 FR 49191. Ortiz is in subgroup I, 351.502(a)(2), and must be ranked on the register. (4) Does not comply. Cutoff 30 days before 2026-10-13 is 2026-09-13; under 351.503(c)(2) no rating put on record after the cutoff may be used, and under 351.503(c)(4) use of ratings must be uniform and consistent within the competitive area. The 2026-10-02 rating must be excluded for every employee, including Pruitt. (5) Does not comply. With two actual ratings, 351.503(f)(2) requires a proxy value equal to the average of the two assigned values: Level 5 (7) and Level 4 (5), proxy 6, total 7+5+6=18, not a presumed Level 3 and not 15. (6) Does not comply. Additional points for exceptional performance are authorized only under 351.503(d) for level-3 employees in a single-pattern system whose highest level is 3, or by transmutation under 351.503(e) in a multiple-pattern area; all employees here are under one five-level pattern, so neither authorizes 2 points for a quality step increase. Advance documentation under 351.503(d)(3)/(e)(1)(ii) does not cure the absence of authority. (7) In order. Where employees in the same tenure group have identical augmented performance credit, are in the same tenure subgroup and have identical service dates and are tied for release, 351.601(c) expressly permits the agency to select any tied employee for release. (8) Does not comply. 351.602(a) prohibits releasing a competing employee while retaining in that level an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion; Reyes, on a temporary promotion ending March 2027, may not be retained while a competing employee is released. (9) In order. Under 351.702(a)(4)(v) an agency need not administer an assessment if, during the 5 years ending on the date the employee receives the notice, the employee occupied the same position (or a position at the same grade/pay level with substantially the same duties, series, qualification requirements and conditions) and received a Level 3-or-higher rating for those duties. Silva held the same position until 2023 and received Level 4 in 2022, within the 5-year period ending 2026-10-13, so no assessment was required. (10) Does not comply. Under 351.702(a)(4)(i)-(iii) the assessment must allow demonstration of job-related skills, be based on a job analysis, and must not consist solely of or principally rely on an automated self-assessment; an automatically scored online self-rating questionnaire does not satisfy this. (11) Does not comply. Under 351.608(a)(3) each temporary exception stands alone and may not be sequenced or stacked; the agency may apply only the exception providing the longest period of retention. Tran may receive one 60-day exception (undue interruption under 351.608(b), max 90 days, or other exceptions under 351.608(g), max 90 days), not 60 days plus a further 60 days. (12) Does not comply. For notices issued on or after 2026-09-02, the appeal lies to OPM, 351.901(a); the notice must state the right to appeal to OPM, the time limit under 351.902(b) and the electronic filing system, 351.802(a)(6) as amended by 2026-15666. A notice telling the employee to appeal to the MSPB is wrong as to forum and omits the required filing information.
Q9.uncertainty: None as to the steps' compliance; the content of notice items 351.802(a)(1),(5) is not printed in the 2026 documents and is not relied on.

Q10.answer: (a) On 2026-09-10 para.(1) of the 330.602 definition of "displaced" contained only the introductory text as revised by the main rule; paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) were absent as published. That is because amendatory instruction 11 of 2026-15665 set out only the introductory text of para.(1) as the revised text, inadvertently deleting (1)(i)-(ii), although OPM intended to revise only the introductory text. (b) The change was made by correcting amendment 2026-18800, 91 FR 58363, published and effective 2026-09-15, restoring (1)(i)-(ii) as they read before 2026-09-02. OPM invoked good cause under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B) to act without notice and comment - no substantive change, restoration of text OPM did not propose or discuss removing, notice therefore unnecessary - and 553(d)(3) for immediate effect. It characterized the document as a correcting amendment making no substantive change. (c) After the change, para.(1)(i) requires receipt of a RIF separation notice under part 351 and that the employee "has not declined an offer under part 351, subpart G...of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high" as the position from which the employee will be separated. Declining an offer of a lower representative rate is not declining a qualifying offer, so Nadia remains "displaced" under (1)(i). If the offered full-time position had the same representative rate (and same schedule) and she declined it, she would have declined a qualifying offer and would not be "displaced" under (1)(i).
Q10.basis: 2026-18800 at 91 FR 58363-58364: Background, Need for Correction, APA discussion, and amended 330.602(1)(i)-(ii); 2026-15665 amendatory instruction 11 at 91 FR 49217 as described in 2026-18800.

Q11.answer: (a) Authority citation, part 351: proposal 5 U.S.C. 1302, 3502, 3503; final adds 1103, 1104, 2301. (b) 351.202(d): proposal broad exclusion from part 351, with (d)(1)(ii)/(d)(2)(i)-(ii) measured "as of the date the agency issues" the notice, (d)(2)(iii) temporary OR TERM appointment under subpart C OR D of part 316, (d)(3) may be actioned "without regard to the provisions of this part"; final narrows to not a "competing employee," removes the issue-date qualifier, limits (d)(2)(iii) to temporary appointment under subpart D, limits (d)(3) to actions for a 351.201(a)(2) reason without standing/order/assignment provided appointment terms and law are respected, and adds (d)(4) modified written notice under 351.801 with 802(a)(1),(3),(5),(6),(b) content, statement of non-competing/non-ranked status, and exception for mere expiration. (c) 351.203: proposal has no "Restoration protected employee" definition; final adds it. Furlough definition: proposal adds "and is instead dependent entirely on congressional action, rather than agency action"; final deletes that phrase. "Rating of record": proposal "assessing performance" and pattern in 430.208(d); final "for performance of" and 430.208(e). (d) 351.204: proposal ends at "reduction in force is necessary"; final adds "and for ensuring that such regulations are administered and applied consistent with all applicable laws, including the merit system principles in 5 U.S.C. 2301(b)." (e) 351.302(d): proposal adverse-action procedures "in part 752 of this chapter"; final "in 5 CFR part 752, if applicable, or other procedures required by law, regulation, or the terms of the employee's appointment." (f) 351.402: proposal revises only (b); final also revises (c), adding the requirement, if the agency establishes or materially modifies a competitive area within 90 days before issuing specific RIF notices for that area, to submit a description and bona fide organizational-basis statement to OPM for advance approval and make them readily available. (g) 351.502: proposal measures subgroups as of the date the agency ISSUES the notice and competitive subgroup II excludes temporary OR TIME-LIMITED appointments under subpart C or D; final measures as of the date the employee RECEIVES the notice and excludes only a temporary appointment under subpart D. (h) 351.503(a)(1): proposal pattern in 430.208(d), Level 2 "Minimally Successful"; final 430.208(e), Level 2 "Minimally Satisfactory." (i) 351.503(b)(2): proposal "in accordance with Sec. 351.501"; final (as corrected) "in accordance with paragraph (a) of this section." 351.503(d)/(e)(2): final adds "as authorized under 430.208(d) prior to the final rule published at 91 FR 41521 (July 7, 2026)" for pattern D/C/G/B/E/F/H references. (j) 351.504(a)(1)-(3): proposal "should be identified" in subgroups AD/A/B; final "must be identified." (k) 351.505(b)(2): proposal credit for retired member "covered by Sec. 351.503(b)"; final "covered by Sec. 351.504(b)." (l) 351.506(c)(1): proposal "their performance credit...and their service computation dates"; final "the employee's performance credit...and the employee's service computation date." 351.506(d): final adds "under this section" and "This paragraph does not limit any right of access available under another statute or regulation." Q13.answer: (1) Erosion of duties. Preamble 91 FR 49190-49191: rule removes the RIF-procedure requirement if the reclassification takes effect after announcement and "the RIF would take effect within 180 days." Text 351.202(c)(3) at 91 FR 49218: agency shall not undertake the reclassification "between the time an agency has formally announced a reduction in force...and the completion of the reduction in force where" it would adversely affect retention standing - no 180-day period, trigger is completion, and an adverse-effect condition is added. Another passage, 91 FR 49191, states the point correctly (announcement to completion, adverse effect). (2) Transfer of function paragraph. Preamble 91 FR 49195: "revising Sec. 351.302(b) to state that, except as permitted in paragraph (e)...the losing agency must use the adverse action procedures in 5 CFR part 752..." Text at 91 FR 49219 places that language in 351.302(d), not (b). No other passage corrects the paragraph. (3) Competitive-area safeguard. Preamble 91 FR 49179 (summary item 3), 49196 and 49203: approval is required when an area "will be in effect less than 90 days" / "has existed for less than 90 days" before notices, and "such approval is also required where an agency materially modifies a competitive area" (no time limit). Text 351.402(c) at 91 FR 49220: approval is required only if the agency establishes OR materially modifies an area "within 90 days before issuing specific reduction in force notices for that competitive area." Period and trigger differ; no passage states the within-90-days limit for material modifications correctly in those passages. (4) Tenure-group definitions. Preamble 91 FR 49196: competitive service tenure group is all competitive employees "who are not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D" as of the date of the RIF notice; excepted group similarly as of the date of the RIF notice. Text 351.203/351.502 at 91 FR 49219-49220: group is subgroups I/II, subgroup is measured as of the date the employee RECEIVES the notice, and competitive subgroup II excludes only a temporary appointment (not time-limited/term) under subpart D. Preamble 91 FR 49191 states the temporary-appointment/subpart D point correctly but repeats the notice-date trigger. (5) Competitive subgroup II date. Preamble 91 FR 49196: subgroup II consists of every other employee "as of the date of the RIF notice." Text 351.502(a)(3) at 91 FR 49220: as of the date the employee receives the notice. Same passage correctly states the receives-date for subgroup I, so the preamble is internally inconsistent. (6) Restoration-protected employee date and period. Preamble 91 FR 49203: employee who, "as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice, remains within the 6-month or 1-year post-reemployment protection period," described as 180 days for service of more than 30 but less than 181 days. Text 351.203 at 91 FR 49219: "as of the date of a specific reduction in force notice, remains entitled under Sec. 353.209(b)...to retention for six (6) months or one (1) year after restoration" - notice date, not receipt date, and six months, not 180 days. (7) Order-of-retention factors in Example 3. Preamble 91 FR 49201: order is "Tenure | Performance...| Vets Pref | Service Computation Date." Text 351.501 at 91 FR 49220: tenure group, then performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference (a combined factor), then tenure subgroup, then SCD. The preamble separates performance and veterans' preference and omits tenure subgroup. Example 2 at 91 FR 49200 states the order correctly. (8) 351.602 prohibition. Preamble 91 FR 49202: OPM is "modifying Sec. 351.602 to remove the prohibition on retaining an employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment" while releasing a competing employee. Text 351.602 at 91 FR 49223 retains the prohibition, reworded as "specifically limited temporary or term promotion" - the prohibition is not removed, and "term" is added. (9) Assessment standard. Preamble 91 FR 49204: assessment "does not rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination." Text 351.702(a)(4)(iii) at 91 FR 49226: assessment "does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment" - an absolute bar in the preamble versus a solely/principally standard in the text.

Q14.answer: (i) Preamble versus regulatory text, OPM appeals rule 2026-15666: (1) 351.901(c)(1) - preamble at 91 FR 49247-49248 and 49244 says "procedures in part 351 are the sole and exclusive means"; text as corrected by 2026-17338 at 91 FR 49263-49264 says "procedures in this subpart are" the sole and exclusive means. The correction changes part to subpart; the preamble retains "part 351." (2) 351.901(b)(1) - preamble at 91 FR 49247 says appellant must prove "the written appeal was timely and in the required form"; text 351.901(b)(1) at 91 FR 49263 requires only "timeliness of the written appeal" - no separate required-form element. (3) 351.902(c)(2) - preamble at 91 FR 49249 says parties "may not electronically file documents or access case materials unless registered as e-filers"; text at 91 FR 49264 adds "or exempted under paragraph (c)(7) of this section for good cause." (4) 351.903(d) - preamble at 91 FR 49250 lists disclosure limits as Privacy Act, classified/national-security, protective orders and other law; text 351.903(d) at 91 FR 49265 also includes "applicable legal privileges." (5) 351.905(b) - preamble at 91 FR 49251 says 5 U.S.C. 554/556/557 do not apply "to an appeal under part 351"; text at 91 FR 49265 says "to an appeal under this subpart." (6) 351.907(a) - preamble at 91 FR 49252 says OPM acts "in its sole discretion"; text at 91 FR 49266 says "sole and exclusive discretion." (7) 351.908 - preamble at 91 FR 49252-49253 says the Director may reopen "any appeal in which OPM has issued a decision that has not yet become final"; text at 91 FR 49266 limits this to "any initial decision or reopened and reconsidered decision." (8) 351.909(e) discussion - preamble at 91 FR 49253 says 351.901(c) makes the OPM process "the sole and exclusive means of appealing covered RIF actions under part 351"; text as corrected is limited to this subpart. (ii) Changes from proposal 2026-02576 to final 2026-15666 not acknowledged in the final rule's summary of changes from proposal at 91 FR 49230-49232: (a) Authority citation: proposal 5 U.S.C. 1302, 3502, 3503; final adds 1103, 1104, 2301 and 38 U.S.C. 4331. (b) 351.802(a)(6): proposal required compliance with Sec. 1201.21; final deletes that sentence (the summary mentions adding time-limit/e-system information but not the deletion; the deletion is discussed later at 91 FR 49247-49248, outside the summary). (c) 351.901(c): proposal superseded appeal procedures in agency policies and CBAs and preserved FLRA jurisdiction; final replaces this with the specific negotiated-grievance/grievance-arbitration bar in (c)(2) and omits FLRA from the preserved-entity list in (c)(3) - the summary lists the preserved entities without noting FLRA's removal. (d) 351.902(c)(2): final adds exemption for good cause under (c)(7). (e) 351.905(c): final adds authority for OPM to "require either party to provide additional information" - the summary's tightening-audit paragraph does not mention this new authority. (f) 351.906(b): proposal "OPM shall" impose sanctions; final "OPM may," and final adds new (c): any sanction must be proportionate, causally related to the violation, and no broader than necessary - neither the shall-to-may change nor new (c) is in the summary (though (c) is discussed at 91 FR 49251-49252). (g) 351.909(c): final provides that if OPM accepts and grants an untimely reconsideration request for good cause, the resulting R&R decision becomes final as in (b) - the summary's finality paragraph states only that an untimely request does not suspend finality. (iii) MSPB inconsistency: MSPB rule 2026-16456 regulatory text at 91 FR 51998 removes 1201.3(a)(6) (RIF) effective 2026-09-02 with no savings clause, while its preamble at 91 FR 51997-51998 states MSPB "will continue to adjudicate" RIF appeals relating to actions taken before OPM's effective date and will accept cases filed after 2026-09-02 where the agency's notice was issued before that date. Within the preamble, the trigger is stated three ways: actions taken before the effective date (91 FR 51997), notice issued before the effective date (91 FR 51997), and RIF effective date preceded 2026-09-02 (91 FR 51998, Sec. III). OPM's rule, by contrast, applies only where the specific RIF notice is issued on or after 2026-09-02 (2026-15666, DATES at 91 FR 49230).

Deciding paragraph 351.504(b)(1)(i) (and (b)(2), pay not based on 20+ years); (b)(4) is satisfied (major, disabled veteran, meets (b)(1)/(2)). D (Master Sergeant, 24 years, length-of-service pay, no disability): NOT a preference eligible, 0 points, Subgroup B - (b)(2) fails (20+ years), (b)(1) and (b)(3) fail, (b)(4)/(5) rank below major. Q5.answer: (a)(i) Notices issued 2026-08-28, before the 2026-09-02 effective date, so the earlier rules apply (2026-15665, DATES). Both career, tenure group I, subgroup B; ranking by adjusted SCD. Old performance credit: Level 3 = 12 years, Level 5 = 20 years (91 FR 49186). Lee: SCD 1998-03-02 minus 12 years = adjusted SCD 1986-03-02. Park: 2019-07-08 minus 20 years = 1999-07-08. Lee ranks higher (earlier adjusted SCD); Park is released. (ii) Notices issued 2026-09-02, on the effective date, so the amended rules apply. Lee: 3+3+3=9. Park: 7+7+7=21. Park ranks higher; Lee is released. (iii) Notices issued 2026-09-03: same as (ii); Lee is released. (b) No. Retention standing is determined as of the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice, 351.507(a); an amended notice issued solely to state a later effective date is not a new specific notice for 351.507 and does not require redetermination or recalculation, 351.805(b). The 2026-10-15 rating therefore does not change standing (the later date only moves the effective date from 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-30). The error-correction duty in 351.507(c) is unaffected but no error is shown. (c) Which version of the rules applies: the date the agency ISSUES the RIF notice (2026-15665 DATES, 91 FR 49178: notice before effective date under old regulations, notice on/after under amended regulations). End of the 4-year ratings period: the date of ISSUANCE of RIF notices, or the agency cutoff date if one is used, 351.503(c)(1)-(2). Tenure subgroup and retention standing: the date the employee RECEIVES the specific RIF notice, 351.502(a)(2)-(3) and 351.507(a).

Q6.answer: (a) Jordan meets 351.701(a): competitive service tenure group employee, current annual rating of record Level 2 (minimally satisfactory) or higher. Assignment rights under 351.701(b): position held by an employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group, not more than 3 grades (or grade intervals) below, qualified under 351.702/703. One-grade interval progression from GS-13: GS-12, GS-11, GS-10 are 1-3 intervals below; GS-9 is 4 below and outside the limit. (1) Ellis GS-12, lower standing - available. (2) Frank GS-11, lower - available. (3) Gale GS-10, lower - available. (4) Hana GS-9, lower but 4 grades below - not available. (5) Ito GS-12, higher standing - not available, 351.701(b)(1). (6) Kim GS-12 part-time - not available, offered position must have the same type of work schedule, 351.701(a). (7) Lund GS-12, different competitive area - not available, must be in the same competitive area, 351.701(a). The agency must offer the position requiring no reduction or the least possible reduction in representative rate among eligible positions, 351.701(a) - the GS-12 held by Ellis. (b) Preference eligible with 30%+ disability: the limit in 351.701(b)(2) becomes 5 grades, so Hana's GS-9 (4 below) becomes available as an assignment-right position, but the mandatory offer remains Ellis's GS-12 as the least-reduction position. (c) Current rating Level 1: 351.701(a) requires Level 2 or higher; Jordan has no assignment right and no position must be offered. (d) Excepted service: 351.701(a) by its terms applies to a competitive service tenure group employee; there is no mandatory assignment right. Under 351.705(a) an agency may at its discretion adopt provisions giving excepted service competing employees assignment rights on the same basis - discretionary only unless the agency has adopted such a provision. (e) The 2026 documents eliminate "bumping" and "retreating" as separate concepts and replace them with a single assignment right to a position held by a lower-standing employee in the same tenure group, 91 FR 49178 summary item 12 and 49204; the former 351.701(d) restriction preventing a Level 2 employee from taking a position held by a higher-rated employee was eliminated, 91 FR 49204, because standing is now the augmented total, not the rating alone. The old handbook's distinction and its Level 2 bar do not reflect the amended rules, although the Level 2 threshold in 351.701(a) remains.
Q6.uncertainty: Whether an agency has adopted discretionary excepted-service assignment rights under 351.705(a) in case (d) cannot be determined from the Federal Register documents.

Q7.answer: (a) Notice issued 2026-08-31, before 2026-09-02: the MSPB hears the appeal. OPM's appeals rule applies only to a RIF action for which the agency issues the specific RIF notice on or after 2026-09-02 (2026-15666 DATES), and the MSPB stated it will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals where the agency's RIF notice was issued before that date (2026-16456 at 91 FR 51997). Documents bearing on the answer: 2026-15666 (OPM RIF Appeals final rule, 91 FR 49230) and 2026-16456 (MSPB Appellate Jurisdiction Update II, 91 FR 51997); the applicability statement in 2026-15666 at 91 FR 49232-49233 is to the same effect. (b) Notice issued 2026-10-19, on/after 2026-09-02: appeal lies to OPM, not the MSPB, 351.901(a). She must file through the electronic filing system identified on OPM's website, 351.902(a),(c). Counting, 351.902(b): appeal within 30 calendar days from the effective date; first day counted is the day after the effective date. Effective Friday 2026-12-18; day 1 = 2026-12-19; day 30 = 2027-01-17 (13 days to 2026-12-31 plus 17 days in January). 2027-01-17 is a Sunday, so under 351.902(b)(1) the period includes the first workday after that date, 2027-01-18, and the appeal is timely if electronically filed by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on that day. (c) She must prove by a preponderance of the evidence: (1) timeliness, (2) OPM jurisdiction, (3) the agency failed to comply with an applicable statute or OPM regulation governing RIFs under part 351, and (4) prejudice - the failure caused her to be subjected to the action or to lose a materially more favorable outcome, 351.901(b). She is not entitled to a hearing as of right: review is based solely on the developed written record unless OPM determines a hearing is necessary and efficient (record insufficient on a material fact, or material witness-credibility dispute), 351.905(c). (d) The rule bars it: 351.901(c)(1)-(2) makes subpart I procedures the sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action under part 351 and provides a RIF action and any matter relating to its appeal "may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration." The preamble at 91 FR 49244-49245 says the rule does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs or adjudicate particular CBA disputes in the rulemaking; when agreements are renegotiated, the governmentwide rule limits the duty and ability to bargain for a conflicting direct RIF appeal process, and questions about existing provisions remain for chapter 71 resolution. (e) No: 351.901(c)(4) - "A party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under this subpart." (f) Yes, she may still appeal: 351.902(b)(3) allows an employee who, before expiration of the filing period, timely filed a complaint/appeal/matter within the independent jurisdiction of an entity in 351.901(c) (OSC is listed) to file a RIF appeal within 30 calendar days after the collateral decision becomes final and is no longer subject to further administrative review, if it materially affects retention standing, order of release, assignment rights or other part 351 rights, as determined by OPM in its sole and exclusive discretion. On the facts - OSC complaint filed before the deadline, final decision 2027-03-10 correcting the rating in a way that would have changed standing - the RIF appeal must be filed within 30 calendar days after 2027-03-10, i.e. by 2027-04-09, 11:59 p.m. ET (subject to the weekend/holiday rule if that date is a Saturday, Sunday or Federal holiday). (g) The deciding provision is the applicability/DATES provision of the OPM appeals rule: 2026-15666, DATES at 91 FR 49230 - "This final rule applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026" - restated in the preamble at 91 FR 49232-49233; the MSPB's parallel statement is at 91 FR 51997.
Q7.uncertainty: Whether 2027-01-18 is a Federal holiday (which would move the (b) deadline to the next workday) is not stated in the Federal Register documents; the count to the first workday after Sunday 2027-01-17 is as stated. The (f) deadline assumes OPM determines the OSC decision materially affects her rights, as the scenario stipulates it would have changed standing.

Q8.answer: (a) The version in force today (2026-11-14) is the pre-2026-10-19 text of 351.806, which the main 2026 RIF rule did not amend; its full text is not printed in the 2026 documents. As described in the administrative-leave rule's preamble, the former paragraph (a) provided the employee would remain in duty status during the notice period "when possible," 91 FR 65926, 65933. The adopted but not yet in-force version, 2026-21320 at 91 FR 65939, effective 2026-11-18, revises 351.806 to: (a) "Under ordinary circumstances, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period"; (b) nothing precludes the agency from placing the employee on administrative leave for all or part of the notice period when the agency determines it is appropriate and consistent with part 630, subpart N; (c) in an emergency lack of work or funds, the agency may place the employee on annual leave with or without consent, on leave without pay with consent, or in nonpay status without consent. (b) Under adopted 351.806(b) employee consent is not required for administrative leave; the agency's determination of appropriateness and consistency with 630 subpart N control. Companion 630.1403(c)(10) at 91 FR 65940 permits administrative leave for RIF-affected employees between receipt of the RIF notice and separation when the agency determines it is in the Government's best interests, "subject to Governmentwide limits established by OPM and agency limits" - the printed text states no fixed number of days for this use. (c) OPM states that its policy guidance already provided that an authorized agency official may provide administrative leave between an employee's receipt of a notice of involuntary separation and the effective date of that separation, and that the new paragraph (b) is consistent with that guidance, 91 FR 65926. (d) No. OPM states the new provisions address only whether an employee may be placed in paid non-duty status during the notice period, do not alter the substantive or procedural requirements governing RIF, and do not authorize bypassing RIF competition, retention registers or appeal rights, 91 FR 65926; retention standing is fixed as of receipt of the notice, 351.507(a).
Q8.basis: 2026-21320 at 91 FR 65924-65940: DATES (eff. 2026-11-18), preamble at 65926 and 65933, regulatory text 351.806 at 65939 and 630.1403(c)(10) at 65940; 2026-15665 regulatory text (no amendment to 351.806) at 91 FR 49218-49227.
Q8.uncertainty: The full text of the currently in-force 351.806 is not printed in the 2026 documents and is not supplied from memory; only the former "when possible" duty-status formulation is described in the 2026 preamble.

Q9.answer: (1) Does not comply in part. Designation/approval by the agency head's designee, not below headquarters level, and chart publication comply with 351.402(b)(1). But the area was designated 2026-08-17, 57 days before notices were issued 2026-10-13, i.e. within 90 days before issuing specific RIF notices; 351.402(c) requires the agency to submit a description and bona fide organizational-basis statement to OPM for approval in advance of the RIF. Nothing was sent to OPM. Required: prior OPM approval with the description and statement, made readily available. (2) In order. A career-conditional employee serving an initial probationary period is not a competing employee, 351.202(d)(2)(ii); the agency may retain such an employee while releasing a competing employee, 351.202(d)(3). (3) Does not comply. "Initial probationary period" does not include the supervisory/managerial probationary period under part 315 subpart I, 351.203; the preamble confirms a career-tenure employee on supervisory probation is included in the RIF in the supervisory position and is not excluded, 91 FR 49191. Ortiz is in subgroup I, 351.502(a)(2), and must be ranked on the register. (4) Does not comply. Cutoff 30 days before 2026-10-13 is 2026-09-13; under 351.503(c)(2) no rating put on record after the cutoff may be used, and under 351.503(c)(4) use of ratings must be uniform and consistent within the competitive area. The 2026-10-02 rating must be excluded for every employee, including Pruitt. (5) Does not comply. With two actual ratings, 351.503(f)(2) requires a proxy value equal to the average of the two assigned values: Level 5 (7) and Level 4 (5), proxy 6, total 7+5+6=18, not a presumed Level 3 and not 15. (6) Does not comply. Additional points for exceptional performance are authorized only under 351.503(d) for level-3 employees in a single-pattern system whose highest level is 3, or by transmutation under 351.503(e) in a multiple-pattern area; all employees here are under one five-level pattern, so neither authorizes 2 points for a quality step increase. Advance documentation under 351.503(d)(3)/(e)(1)(ii) does not cure the absence of authority. (7) In order. Where employees in the same tenure group have identical augmented performance credit, are in the same tenure subgroup and have identical service dates and are tied for release, 351.601(c) expressly permits the agency to select any tied employee for release. (8) Does not comply. 351.602(a) prohibits releasing a competing employee while retaining in that level an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion; Reyes, on a temporary promotion ending March 2027, may not be retained while a competing employee is released. (9) In order. Under 351.702(a)(4)(v) an agency need not administer an assessment if, during the 5 years ending on the date the employee receives the notice, the employee occupied the same position (or a position at the same grade/pay level with substantially the same duties, series, qualification requirements and conditions) and received a Level 3-or-higher rating for those duties. Silva held the same position until 2023 and received Level 4 in 2022, within the 5-year period ending 2026-10-13, so no assessment was required. (10) Does not comply. Under 351.702(a)(4)(i)-(iii) the assessment must allow demonstration of job-related skills, be based on a job analysis, and must not consist solely of or principally rely on an automated self-assessment; an automatically scored online self-rating questionnaire does not satisfy this. (11) Does not comply. Under 351.608(a)(3) each temporary exception stands alone and may not be sequenced or stacked; the agency may apply only the exception providing the longest period of retention. Tran may receive one 60-day exception (undue interruption under 351.608(b), max 90 days, or other exceptions under 351.608(g), max 90 days), not 60 days plus a further 60 days. (12) Does not comply. For notices issued on or after 2026-09-02, the appeal lies to OPM, 351.901(a); the notice must state the right to appeal to OPM, the time limit under 351.902(b) and the electronic filing system, 351.802(a)(6) as amended by 2026-15666. A notice telling the employee to appeal to the MSPB is wrong as to forum and omits the required filing information.

Q10.answer: (a) On 2026-09-10 para.(1) of the 330.602 definition of "displaced" contained only the introductory text as revised by the main rule; paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) were absent as published. That is because amendatory instruction 11 of 2026-15665 set out only the introductory text of para.(1) as the revised text, inadvertently deleting (1)(i)-(ii), although OPM intended to revise only the introductory text. (b) The change was made by correcting amendment 2026-18800, 91 FR 58363, published and effective 2026-09-15, restoring (1)(i)-(ii) as they read before 2026-09-02. OPM invoked good cause under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B) to act without notice and comment - no substantive change, restoration of text OPM did not propose or discuss removing, notice therefore unnecessary - and 553(d)(3) for immediate effect. It characterized the document as a correcting amendment making no substantive change. (c) After the change, para.(1)(i) requires receipt of a RIF separation notice under part 351 and that the employee "has not declined an offer under part 351, subpart G...of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high" as the position from which the employee will be separated. Declining an offer of a lower representative rate is not declining a qualifying offer, so Nadia remains "displaced" under (1)(i). If the offered full-time position had the same representative rate (and same schedule) and she declined it, she would have declined a qualifying offer and would not be "displaced" under (1)(i).

(m) 351.604: proposal revises (b) and removes (d) for RIF furloughs; final does not amend 351.604 at all. (n) 351.605: proposal combines abolishment and notice in (a)-(b) with notice content 802(a)(1),(3),(5),(6),(b); final restructures into (a)-(d), adds (c) written notice under 351.801, identification of the area, express statement that the employee was not ranked, notice not required to include 802(a)(2) or (a)(4), and (d) retention register not required and assignment rights must not be applied. (p) 351.608(a)(2): proposal CTAP under part 330 subpart E; final subpart F. (q) 351.701(a): Level 2 "minimally successful" in proposal, "minimally satisfactory" in final. (r) 351.702(a)(4)(iii): proposal "does not solely include or principally rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination"; final "does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment." 351.702(a)(4) final adds new (v): no assessment required if, during the 5 years ending on the date the employee receives the notice, the employee occupied the same position or a position at the same grade/pay level with substantially the same duties, series, qualification requirements and conditions and received Level 3 or higher for those duties. (s) 351.802(a)(2): proposal "veteran status"; final "veterans' preference subgroup." (a)(3): proposal "link to part 351 of this chapter and access to the agency's records"; final "link to 5 CFR part 351 and information on how to access the agency's records." Final also adds introductory text to 802(a). Q13.answer: (1) Erosion of duties. Preamble 91 FR 49190-49191: rule removes the RIF-procedure requirement if the reclassification takes effect after announcement and "the RIF would take effect within 180 days." Text 351.202(c)(3) at 91 FR 49218: agency shall not undertake the reclassification "between the time an agency has formally announced a reduction in force...and the completion of the reduction in force where" it would adversely affect retention standing - no 180-day period, trigger is completion, and an adverse-effect condition is added. Another passage, 91 FR 49191, states the point correctly (announcement to completion, adverse effect). (2) Transfer of function paragraph. Preamble 91 FR 49195: "revising Sec. 351.302(b) to state that, except as permitted in paragraph (e)...the losing agency must use the adverse action procedures in 5 CFR part 752..." Text at 91 FR 49219 places that language in 351.302(d), not (b). No other passage corrects the paragraph. (3) Competitive-area safeguard. Preamble 91 FR 49179 (summary item 3), 49196 and 49203: approval is required when an area "will be in effect less than 90 days" / "has existed for less than 90 days" before notices, and "such approval is also required where an agency materially modifies a competitive area" (no time limit). Text 351.402(c) at 91 FR 49220: approval is required only if the agency establishes OR materially modifies an area "within 90 days before issuing specific reduction in force notices for that competitive area." Period and trigger differ; no passage states the within-90-days limit for material modifications correctly in those passages. (4) Tenure-group definitions. Preamble 91 FR 49196: competitive service tenure group is all competitive employees "who are not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D" as of the date of the RIF notice; excepted group similarly as of the date of the RIF notice. Text 351.203/351.502 at 91 FR 49219-49220: group is subgroups I/II, subgroup is measured as of the date the employee RECEIVES the notice, and competitive subgroup II excludes only a temporary appointment (not time-limited/term) under subpart D. Preamble 91 FR 49191 states the temporary-appointment/subpart D point correctly but repeats the notice-date trigger. (5) Competitive subgroup II date. Preamble 91 FR 49196: subgroup II consists of every other employee "as of the date of the RIF notice." Text 351.502(a)(3) at 91 FR 49220: as of the date the employee receives the notice. Same passage correctly states the receives-date for subgroup I, so the preamble is internally inconsistent. (6) Restoration-protected employee date and period. Preamble 91 FR 49203: employee who, "as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice, remains within the 6-month or 1-year post-reemployment protection period," described as 180 days for service of more than 30 but less than 181 days. Text 351.203 at 91 FR 49219: "as of the date of a specific reduction in force notice, remains entitled under Sec. 353.209(b)...to retention for six (6) months or one (1) year after restoration" - notice date, not receipt date, and six months, not 180 days. (7) Order-of-retention factors in Example 3. Preamble 91 FR 49201: order is "Tenure | Performance...| Vets Pref | Service Computation Date." Text 351.501 at 91 FR 49220: tenure group, then performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference (a combined factor), then tenure subgroup, then SCD. The preamble separates performance and veterans' preference and omits tenure subgroup. Example 2 at 91 FR 49200 states the order correctly. (8) 351.602 prohibition. Preamble 91 FR 49202: OPM is "modifying Sec. 351.602 to remove the prohibition on retaining an employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment" while releasing a competing employee. Text 351.602 at 91 FR 49223 retains the prohibition, reworded as "specifically limited temporary or term promotion" - the prohibition is not removed, and "term" is added. (9) Assessment standard. Preamble 91 FR 49204: assessment "does not rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination." Text 351.702(a)(4)(iii) at 91 FR 49226: assessment "does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment" - an absolute bar in the preamble versus a solely/principally standard in the text.

Q14.answer: (i) Preamble versus regulatory text, OPM appeals rule 2026-15666: (1) 351.901(c)(1) - preamble at 91 FR 49247-49248 and 49244 says "procedures in part 351 are the sole and exclusive means"; text as corrected by 2026-17338 at 91 FR 49263-49264 says "procedures in this subpart are" the sole and exclusive means.
